events.text: JPM internet preview for 1Q26: estimate setup and framing of the capex guide as the central theme heading into the print.

BofA/Fenske (spec-sales): META screened as the cheapest Mag7 name on relative forward P/E following the social-media litigation selloff, with the best post-earnings revisions in the group and untapped consumer-AI optionality across IG/WhatsApp/FB.

BofA/Fenske preview: expected a beat (Street rev $55.4B, ~70% performance ads), with Muse Spark targeting frontier quality by year-end; a capex guide raise framed as a "non-event" vs MSFT/GOOG/AMZN, but META still lacks the enterprise/cloud re-rate thesis.

Q1 FY26: revenue $56.3B +33% y/y (+29% cc); FoA ad rev $55.0B +33%; impressions +19%, price/ad +12%. Op income $22.9B (41% margin); clean EPS $7.31. Capex $19.8B; FY26 guide raised to $125-145B (memory pricing). Q2 revenue guide $58-61B.

Expert recap: META was the only big-three to flag macro — an ad-spend deceleration in March (Middle East, US/W Europe), recovering in April; still printed ~33%, ~1.5pts below the top of the guide. The first full quarter of EU "less-personalized-ads" regulation exposes ~16% of ad revenue.
BofA/Wigg (spec-sales): META remains a "show-me story" that needs a "wow" product shipped to re-rate vs the easier capex justification at GOOG/MSFT/AMZN.

Nowak (MS, OW PT $775): META is his #1 pick in the Mag7 — "a deep freaking moat" (3.5B DAU). Catalysts: a personal/shoppable agent ("Meta Claw"/Muse); ad rev could grow ~20-25% in '27 on algo improvement alone. Neocloud as "backup optionality" (~$10B/GW) = 8%+ of upside to '28 EPS.

Jefferies conf: a CIO said he would bring Meta into his enterprise environment IF Meta launched a commercial model wrapper/cloud (Red Hat-style) — framed as underpriced bull optionality; the absence of such a vehicle is precisely why it does not get a GOOG-style re-rate.

BofA equity call: the bull emphasizes that the 33% growth is pre-AI-product (Muse Spark NOT yet in the ads/reco stack). Bears (buy-side PMs): ~$30B of capex to ~$150B for ~10pts of incremental growth, incremental ROIC "deeply negative," the MSL lab as a hidden loss of ~$40B/year through '27; no enterprise/cloud story to re-rate on.

JPM: FY26 capex midpoint raised +$10bn to $135bn (memory cost); models ~$185bn FY27E / ~$225bn FY28E. FCF turns negative, cumulative funding gap ~$97bn over 3 years; contractual commitments +$107bn in the quarter to $238bn; 20% Hyperion stake with ~$28bn of RVG. Returned to the bond market with a $25bn deal.
JPM: Broadcom planning multiple gigawatts of MTIA deployments starting in 2027; Meta intends to train its next-generation models on MTIA — corroborates the >1GW in-house ASIC ramp.

UBS/Ben Legg: increasingly excited about Meta Business Agents as the biggest 5-year tailwind — a SaaS layer ($15 and $50/month, free today). Models a ~1-2pt tailwind already in Q4, lifting FY ad growth to ~30-31%; micro-businesses ~$1.5T of ad spend by 2030, with Meta capturing ~$200B.

UBS/Vayner Media (ad-agency): digital spend is a "tale of two cities" — efficiency cleanup everywhere funding continued scale in the walled gardens (Google/Meta/TikTok/Amazon) at the expense of everyone else.

UBS/Scott Linzer (agency checks): more skeptical on the core — total Meta Q2 1.4-1.5% / Q3 3.4% / Q4 4.5-5% / FY ~4%; Meta pricing flat-to-up (it does not fall like Google's CPCs) is the key hesitation; Instagram materially underperforming; Meta Business AI "not ready for prime time," more of a 2027 opportunity.

'The Paths to 25-50% GenAI ROIC' — Overweight and Top Pick, PT $775 on a DCF / long-term EBITDA multiple at ~8% WACC and ~3% terminal growth, implying ~23x '27 P/E (thesis 'The Age of Efficiency'); bull $1,000 (~29x blended '27/'28), bear $450 (~15x, explicitly naming 'higher capital intensity from mis-execution around the data center build widens losses with minimal ROIC'). Spot $595.19, mean consensus PT $823.38 (range $664.46-$1,015), 88% OW; options-implied (24 Jul 2026) P(>$775) ~17.9% vs P(<$450) ~27.6% — the market prices the bear at ~1.5x the base. cc revenue growth 22.5% (2025) → 26.0% (26e) → 22.0% (27e) → 19.8% (28e). The quantified Muse-API leg is framework #2, a model-enabled API on OWNED infrastructure: 65% of 1GW of GB300 to inference at 2,750 tokens/sec/GPU and $1.75/mn blended → $30bn revenue/GW, $22.7bn incremental EBIT (~75% margin), $17.9bn NOPAT, ~46% ROIC (band 19-63%) — the best returns of the three models MS builds, and MS's $1.75/mn reference price is itself benchmarked to 'Muse Spark 1.1 blended pricing $1.58 (8K/1K I/O),' i.e. the Street's reference price for the whole GenAI-API economy is now Meta's own model. Worth flagging because it sits inside the bull's own model: MS's key-earnings-inputs table has GAAP operating income at 83,276 (2025) → 92,216 (26e) → 101,748 (27e) → 104,841 (28e) — +10.7% / +10.3% / only +3.0% — against ~20% cc revenue growth in 2028, the depreciation wall from MS's own $225bn/$250bn '27/'28 capex path landing in the P&L. MS is above consensus on FY26e revenue (254,653 vs 253,077) and EBITDA (148,034 vs 142,872) but BELOW on EPS (32.49 vs 32.95). So the Top Pick rests on call options MS states are NOT in the base numbers — AI-driven upside, subscription adoption, click-to-message.

Jefferies AI Summit recap: META a summit top pick as the 'personal agents' beneficiary; Muse users 'have passed 500K after only a couple of weeks' (Notable Capital: 250-500K) vs hundreds of millions on IG; rising consumer familiarity with personal agents should drive business AI adoption and extend the compute cycle beyond 2028-29. Counter from expert Bill MacCartney: winner-take-one market decided by trust and data access, META's trust issues could limit it as the primary agent. BUY, no PT in the note.

GS hyperscaler ROIC framework, META row (Exhibit 15): CY26-27 AI-compute capex $308,677mn -> 7GW (illustrative) -> $253,033mn of cumulative CY28-30 revenue required for a 15% ROIC (~$11.60bn/GW/yr; $83.2bn/$84.7bn/$85.1bn in 2028/29/30 at 60/80/85% utilisation), EBIT $87.9bn (34.7%), D&A $49.4bn/yr; assumptions ~$42bn/GW, $836mn/GW opex, 70/30 compute/shell. Six-company aggregate ~$1.42trn / 41GW. Press reports: META ~7GW by YE26, ~14GW by YE27. Buy / PT $725 restated. A hurdle, not a forecast.

Skift travel-forum read-through: EXPE confirmed it will remain merchant of record in any transactions initiated by Muse and is engaging GOOGL/OpenAI/META to be an early agent partner; BKNG argues travelers may still prefer to book on its own sites for trust and customer service.

events.text: 61pp retail/consumer note 'Muse: Rewriting the Retail/Consumer Playbook': Muse is 'the most credible agentic threat we have seen to date' because capability is paired with Meta's consumer data. The transaction is defensible (retailer 'handshake' agents keep checkout and data); discovery is not - advertising dollars 'will need to follow the consumer to these new interfaces', retail media the exposed line. META a 'differentiated winner'; 11 announced retailer connectors (Walmart, Best Buy, American Eagle, DICK'S, Fanatics, Gap, Michael Kors, Sephora, Ulta, Wayfair + Instacart); Stripe Link payments, Shop Pay coming; initial take rates near zero; top-5 downloaded app through ~3 weeks; free tier ~100+ queries/day. Watch a GOOGL agent around Gemini 4 in 4Q and an AAPL agent powered by GOOGL. OW by disclosure; no PT printed.

'Apps, Agents, and Aggregation': Meta provisions every US Muse user a 2-core / 8GB RAM / 8GB storage VM - 'the only way to make agents work for most people'. Agents make doing things abundant, so the scarce thing is volition/inspiration; apps become suppliers to the agent as publications were to Aggregators. Muse and Microsoft's new Copilot are bidding to be both platform and Aggregator; most people will have one agent; 'Meta reaches nearly every person on earth; Microsoft reaches nearly every employee.' Meta's devices are 'Muse delivery mechanisms'.

META hires MongoDB CEO CJ Desai to build an 'Enterprise Platform'; MDB down as much as 20% intraday. Bernstein's software team: 'History isn't kind to consumer internet leaders entering software' - no material precedent (AWS/GCP are IaaS; Dropbox/Canva never broke into enterprise; META's own Facebook for Business / Workplace); needs a ground-up product, a separate R&D function and an enterprise sales motion into buyers already owned by competitors; the PaaS route means open-source-derived offerings, war with Amazon and Google, and enterprise data that resides mostly at Microsoft. No change to Bernstein software models, PTs or ratings; no META view.
